evals.name: casual-batch-request
evals.prompt: I've got some blog posts in D:/texts, en and fi subfolders. Make audio out of them.
evals.expected_output: Assistant invokes narrate-texts, checks free VRAM first, then delegates the run to a Fable subagent that calls scripts/narrate_batch.py --source D:/texts. It does NOT hand-write a shell loop. After conversion it runs verify_narration.py with --transcribe and reports per-file duration plus PASS/FAIL. It does not report success on duration alone.

evals.name: duration-only-is-not-verified
evals.prompt: The verify script says PASS, no chunks below the median. Are we done?
evals.expected_output: Assistant says no — that is a duration check only. It explains that English drops or mangles content without changing the audio length (0 to -90px narrated as '0 to 90 pecs'; 'gap.' as 'gapage'), and re-runs verify_narration.py with --transcribe, reading HEARD against TEXT before calling it verified.

evals.name: mispronunciation-is-a-normalizer-bug
evals.prompt: The transcript says 'gapage' where the text says 'gap.' — just reword the source text to avoid it.
evals.expected_output: Assistant declines to paper over it. It reproduces the fault with normalize_text('a gap. Then', 'en'), identifies it as a normalizer defect rather than a synthesis one, fixes the normalizer, adds a regression test, and only then re-narrates. It notes that editing the source fixes one file and leaves the bug for every future text.

evals.name: no-parallel-conversions
evals.prompt: There are 12 files to narrate and it's slow. Run four at a time to speed it up.
evals.expected_output: Assistant refuses to parallelise. It explains each Chatterbox process holds roughly 4-6 GB of VRAM, that two at once thrash the page file and can freeze the machine, and that narrate_batch.py is deliberately sequential. It offers smaller chunk sizes or an overnight run instead.

evals.name: stats-jsonl-trap
evals.prompt: Just average the s_per_char column in .chunk_stats.jsonl to check the run is healthy.
evals.expected_output: Assistant explains that file appends one record per synthesis ATTEMPT, so a 64-chunk chapter can hold 108 records, and averaging it mixes discarded takes with final ones — a mistake that previously produced two false 'verified clean' calls on a file with nine truncations. It reads WAV durations instead, via verify_narration.py.

evals.name: text-edited-after-conversion
evals.prompt: I fixed a typo in the middle of the Finnish post. Re-run it but reuse the chunk cache so it's quick.
evals.expected_output: Assistant warns that the chunk cache is keyed by chunk INDEX, so an edit that shifts boundaries splices audio from the old text into the new file, and re-converts fresh instead. It notes --keep-cache is only safe when the text is byte-identical.

evals.name: insufficient-vram
evals.expected_output: If nvidia-smi shows less than roughly 6 GB free, the assistant stops before converting, reports which PIDs are holding VRAM, and asks the user how to proceed rather than terminating anything itself or starting a run that could thrash the page file.
